draft.emotion: encouraging and patient, explaining something clearly to someone
notes: Causative form of पढ़ना (paṛhnā, to read/study). The person being taught is marked with को (ko): बच्चों को पढ़ाना (to teach children).
Used for academic subjects and reading (हिंदी पढ़ाना, to teach Hindi). For practical skills like swimming, driving, or cooking, use सिखाना (sikhānā) instead.

senses.definition: To instruct someone in an academic subject or lesson, or to tutor.

examples.emotion: proud and steady, stating someone's profession

examples.text: वह शाम को बच्चों को पढ़ाती है।
examples.translation: She tutors children in the evening.

draftBefore.shortGloss: to teach; to help someone learn
draftBefore.emotion: encouraging and patient, explaining something clearly to someone
notes: प पढ़ाना (paṛānā) is the causative form of पढ़ना (paṛnā, to study/read). It requires the agent to be marked with से (se) when indicating who is being helped to learn or taught.
Do not confuse with सिखाना (sikhānā), which often means to teach a practical skill or habit, whereas पढ़ाना leans more towards academic subjects or structured instruction.

senses.definition: To impart knowledge or instruct someone in a subject, skill, or lesson.

examples.text: वह स्कूल में हिंदी पढ़ाता है।
examples.emotion: proud and steady, stating someone's profession

senses.definition: To guide and help someone understand a topic or learn something new.

examples.text: क्या तुम मुझे सवाल हल करना पढ़ा सकते हो?
